files.Snabb Fakta || 3 DAGAR ENSAM UNDER VATTN:
1
00:00:50,440 --> 00:01:02,860
This got the boat to edge and it was turned upside down in the water and now began to sink down to the bottom.

2
00:01:06,420 --> 00:01:17,060
Water poured in everywhere and the panic looked into the crew that was locked up in its cabins at this time.

3
00:01:17,060 --> 00:01:20,060
Why were they locked up?

4
00:01:20,060 --> 00:01:29,980
Well, because the area they were on used to be regularly affected by pirates who rob and sometimes steal the ships.

5
00:01:29,980 --> 00:01:37,780
It was a security measure so that they would not be injured or ended up hostage to the pirates.

6
00:01:37,780 --> 00:01:43,000
Unfortunately, this security measure became their death.

7
00:01:43,000 --> 00:01:50,100
But not for the boat's chef Harrison Olene, 29 years.

8
00:01:50,100 --> 00:01:56,960
He was in the toilet when all this happened and suddenly feels how the boat turns.

9
00:01:58,500 --> 00:02:08,680
He is thrown out from the toilet and around the different spaces in the boat while at the same time becomes darker and darker

10
00:02:48,380 --> 00:03:03,980
After all, when we humans breathe in, we breathe in oxygen, but when we exhale, the lungs emit a gas called carbon dioxide.

11
00:03:04,000 --> 00:03:14,300
Slowly but surely, the air bubble would be filled with more and more carbon dioxide and in the end Harrison would die from it.

12
00:03:14,300 --> 00:03:26,140
The air bubble had enough volume to make the oxygen last for about 60 hours before he would start to suffer carbon dioxide poisoning.

13
00:03:26,140 --> 00:03:30,880
However, this was not something he himself knew about at this time.

14
00:03:32,640 --> 00:03:45,900
In total darkness, Harrison manages to tear off some wooden panels from the walls and finds a mattress that he could use to build a small platform that he could sit on.

15
00:03:45,900 --> 00:03:49,340
And there he would be sitting.

16
00:03:49,340 --> 00:03:59,820
Dressed in only their underwear in the cold sea water, without food or fresh water to drink and in a cold and wet room

17
00:03:59,820 --> 00:04:11,900
With a slow but surely declining oxygen supply and in total darkness, Harrison seemed to survive not so great.

18
00:04:11,900 --> 00:04:14,900
Hour after hour passed.

19
00:04:14,960 --> 00:04:18,640
Every little sound scared him.

20
00:05:38,300 --> 00:05:47,020
The diver had not expected anyone to survive and Harrison had almost given up hope of being saved.

21
00:05:49,860 --> 00:05:59,920
Unfortunately, after Harrison spent almost 3 days at 30 meters depth, he could not only take him to the surface.

22
00:05:59,920 --> 00:06:11,520
There is something called scuba diving, or even "pressure drop" that can occur in all people who are suddenly exposed to a pressure cut.

23
00:06:11,520 --> 00:06:22,420
When you dive, the body's different tissues absorb nitrogen from the breathing air which is in proportion to the pressure in the environment.

24
00:06:22,420 --> 00:06:33,180
This is no problem as long as you stay at the same depth or the same pressure, but the problem arises when the pressure is reduced too quickly.

25
00:06:33,180 --> 00:06:41,700
The nitrogen inside the body then turns to a gaseous form and forms bubbles in the tissues and blood.

26
00:06:41,700 --> 00:06:54,880
It can lead to loss of sensation, paralysis and even brain damage.
In the worst case, this leads to a coma and that the person dies.

27
00:06:54,880 --> 00:07:08,260
Harrison had to spend about 2 and a half days in a decompression chamber to get used to his body at the pressure on the surface.

28
00:07:12,640 --> 00:07:17,860
Harrison had no idea how long he had been down in the boat.

29
00:07:17,860 --> 00:07:30,280
He guessed in 12 hours and was very surprised that he almost spent 3 days all by himself in total darkness.

30
00:07:30,280 --> 00:07:37,380
Harrison is very grateful that he survived but is still plagued by nightmares.

1
00:00:50,440 --> 00:01:02,860
Det här fick båten att kantra och den vändes upp och ner i vattnet och började nu att sjunka ner till botten.

2
00:01:06,420 --> 00:01:17,060
Vatten strömmade in överallt och paniken letade sig in hos besättningen som var inlåsta i sina hytter vid det här tillfället.

3
00:01:17,060 --> 00:01:20,060
Varför var de inlåsta?

4
00:01:20,060 --> 00:01:29,980
Jo, för att området som de befann sig på brukade regelbundet drabbas av pirater som rånar och ibland stjäl skeppen.

5
00:01:29,980 --> 00:01:37,780
Det var en säkerhetsåtgärd så att de inte skulle bli skadade eller hamna som gisslan hos piraterna.

6
00:01:37,780 --> 00:01:43,000
Tyvärr så blev den här säkerhetsåtgärden deras död.

7
00:01:43,000 --> 00:01:50,100
Men inte för båtens kock Harrison Okene, 29 år.

8
00:01:50,100 --> 00:01:56,960
Han var på toaletten när allt det här hände och känner plötsligt hur båten vänder på sig.

9
00:01:58,500 --> 00:02:08,680
Han kastas ut från toaletten och runt om i de olika utrymmena i båten medan det samtidigt blir mörkare och mörkare

10
00:02:48,380 --> 00:03:03,980
Det är ju nämligen så att när vi människor andas in så andas vi in syre, men när vi andas ut så släpper lungorna ut en gas som kallas för koldioxid.

11
00:03:04,000 --> 00:03:14,300
Sakta men säkert så skulle luftbubblan fyllas med mer och mer koldioxid och till slut så skulle Harrison dö av det.

12
00:03:14,300 --> 00:03:26,140
Luftbubblan hade tillräckligt stor volym för att syret skulle räcka i ca 60 timmar innan han skulle börja drabbas av koldioxidförgiftning.

13
00:03:26,140 --> 00:03:30,880
Detta var dock inget som han själv visste om vid det här tillfället.

14
00:03:32,640 --> 00:03:45,900
I totalt mörker så lyckas Harrison slita av några träpaneler från väggarna och hittar en madrass som han kunde använda för att bygga en liten plattform som han kunde sitta på.

15
00:03:45,900 --> 00:03:49,340
Och där skulle han bli sittande.

16
00:03:49,340 --> 00:03:59,820
Klädd i endast sina kalsonger i det kalla havsvattnet, utan mat eller färskt vatten att dricka och i ett kallt och blött rum

17
00:03:59,820 --> 00:04:11,900
med en sakta men säkert minskande syretillförsel och i totalt mörker så verkade Harrisons chanser att överleva inte så stora.

18
00:04:11,900 --> 00:04:14,900
Timme efter timme gick.

19
00:04:14,960 --> 00:04:18,640
Varje litet ljud skrämde honom.

20
00:05:38,300 --> 00:05:47,020
Dykaren hade inte förväntat sig att någon hade överlevt  och Harrison hade nästan gett upp hoppet om att bli räddad.

21
00:05:49,860 --> 00:05:59,920
Efter att Harrison spenderat nästan 3 dagar på 30 meters djup så kunde man tyvärr inte bara ta upp honom till ytan.

22
00:05:59,920 --> 00:06:11,520
Det finns nämligen något som kallas för Dykarsjuka, eller också “Tryckfallssjuka” som kan uppstå hos alla människor som plötsligt utsätts för en trycksänkning.

23
00:06:11,520 --> 00:06:22,420
När man dyker så absorberar kroppens olika vävnader kväve från andningsluften som ligger i proportion till trycket i omgivningen.

24
00:06:22,420 --> 00:06:33,180
Det här är inget problem så länge man stannar kvar på samma djup eller samma tryck, men problemet uppstår när trycket minskas för snabbt.

25
00:06:33,180 --> 00:06:41,700
Kvävet inne i kroppen övergår då till en gasform och bildar bubblor i vävnaderna och blodet.

26
00:06:41,700 --> 00:06:54,880
Det kan leda till känselbortfall, förlamning och även hjärnskador.
I värsta fall så detta leda till koma och att personen avlider.

27
00:06:54,880 --> 00:07:08,260
Harrison fick spendera ungefär 2 och en halv dagar dagar i en dekompressionskammare för att vänja tillbaka hans kropp vid trycket på ytan.

28
00:07:12,640 --> 00:07:17,860
Harrison hade ingen aning om hur länge han hade varit nere i båten.

29
00:07:17,860 --> 00:07:30,280
Han gissade på 12 timmar och blev väldigt förvånad över att han nästan spenderat 3 dagar helt själv i totalt mörker.

30
00:07:30,280 --> 00:07:37,380
Harrison är väldigt tacksam över att han överlevde men plågas fortfarande av mardrömmar.

files.Snabb Fakta || BRANDEN PÅ M⧸S SCANDINAVI:
1
00:01:41,716 --> 00:01:50,550
The ship left the port of Oslo at 21:45 local time - 2 hours and a quarter delayed.

2
00:01:50,550 --> 00:02:01,666
The journey would have started already at 19:30, but work on boarding passenger cars and trucks took longer than expected.

3
00:02:01,666 --> 00:02:14,683
The journey to Fredrikshamn goes painlessly at first until it was between 01: 45-02: 00 on the night of April 7.

4
00:02:14,683 --> 00:02:27,100
The ship was now out on open water in a part of the North Sea called Skagerack and most of the passengers were sleeping.

5
00:02:28,583 --> 00:02:37,616
On deck 4, some passengers are suddenly awakened from their sleep when they hear a crackling sound out in the corridor.

6
00:02:37,616 --> 00:02:49,216
A few doors away is a pile of bedding on the floor that burns.
Fortunately, they manage to extinguish the fire together with the crew.

7
00:02:49,216 --> 00:02:57,066
One of the crew members went up to the command bridge and announced the first mate who at that time had the guard.

8
00:02:57,066 --> 00:03:07,766
He in turn went and announced to the captain of what had happened and told the captain that "someone is playing Pyroman".

9
00:03:07,766 --> 00:03:17,100
After captain Hugo Larsen was announced, the first mate was sent down to the fire site to check.

10
00:03:17,100 --> 00:03:28,783
It was made sure to be properly extinguished and cleaned up.
After that, the first mate called the captain on the bridge again and announced that everything was under control.

11
00:03:29,700 --> 00:03:44,100
But it all didn't end there.
Sometime just after 02:00, one more fire arose on deck 3 outside a cabin in a corridor on the starboard side.

12
00:03:44,100 --> 00:03:57,316
This was near the stairs leading up to tires 4 and 5. Within a few minutes, the fire had spread so much that the entire corridor was in flames

13
00:03:57,316 --> 00:04:05,066
And thick smoke looked up the stairwell and began to fill the corridors on tires 4 and 5.

14
00:04:05,066 --> 00:04:15,350
There were alarms from a number of different fire alarms in the corridors on decks 4 and 5 when the passengers there had discovered the fire.

15
00:04:15,350 --> 00:04:31,200
When the captain learned about this it was around 02:15 and when the first mate entered the bridge he received orders from the captain to send out the signal "fire alarm" all over the ship.

16
00:04:31,200 --> 00:04:41,116
The captain triggered the self -closure of the fire doors in the areas where the fire alarm buttons had been pressed by the passengers.

17
00:04:41,116 --> 00:04:51,883
But since no button had been pressed in where the fire started on the starboard side by deck 3, the fire doors were left open there.

18
00:04:51,883 --> 00:05:05,033
The walls and ceiling on deck 3 were covered with plastic laminate and when it burned there it created a smoke that contained high levels of hydrogen cyanide and carbon monoxide

19
00:05:05,033 --> 00:05:14,033
And after only 10 minutes, the corridors had reached a deadly concentration of the two gases.

20
00:05:16,983 --> 00:05:28,366
At 02:24 they now turned off the ship's propulsion and then started the fire pumps but the fire was already out of control.

21
00:05:28,366 --> 00:05:42,583
Captain Hugo Larsen sent out an emergency signal to Tjøme Radio in Norway, announcing the fire on board and that the passengers and crew would now start moving towards the lifeboats.

22
00:05:43,183 --> 00:05:51,533
On board, there is currently total panic among passengers.
Many are struggling through the smoke -filled corridors.

23
00:05:51,533 --> 00:05:59,883
Some people have already died of the toxic smoke and passengers may step over them in order to reach.

24
00:09:37,700 --> 00:09:44,533
159 people lost their lives that night.

25
00:09:51,833 --> 00:09:59,833
The investigations conducted afterwards by the forensic authorities show they probably died quickly.

26
00:09:59,833 --> 00:10:13,766
It was a combination of a number of causes, partly the fire itself but also of high carbon dioxide content as well as the toxic smoke containing carbon monoxide and hydrogen cyanide.

27
00:10:13,766 --> 00:10:24,750
It is estimated that the passengers who made their way out into the corridors had not been able to get to any exit before collapsing on the floor.

28
00:10:24,750 --> 00:10:31,166
Most of the dead, which were 99 people, remained in their cabins.

29
00:10:31,166 --> 00:10:38,683
About 50 people were found in the corridors and most were in aft on deck 5.

30
00:10:38,683 --> 00:10:48,233
323 people were rescued from Scandinavian Star that night and only about 30 were injured.

31
00:10:48,233 --> 00:10:55,666
Most had mild smoke poisoning or other lighter injuries such as splits and bruises.

32
00:10:55,666 --> 00:11:05,683
Some were taken ashore via helicopter and others were brought with the vessels to Lysekil, Sandefjord, Fredriksstad and Fredrikshamn.

33
00:11:07,133 --> 00:11:18,083
11.55 During the day, Scandinavian Star was towed to Lysekil and is 21:17 in the evening.

34
00:11:18,083 --> 00:11:29,516
The day after April 8 at 16:30, the fire is finally extinguished and the dead can start to be lifted ashore.

35
00:11:29,516 --> 00:11:42,816
Since the majority of passengers were from Norway, the dead bodies were transported in large white cooling cars with police cards to the Forensic Institute in Oslo.

36
00:11:43,750 --> 00:11:54,233
Two questions quickly appear in the head.
Who built the fires and why did everything go ... so wrong?

37
00:11:54,233 --> 00:12:00,733
Sadly, it has not been possible to determine who or who built the fires on the ship.

38
00:12:00,733 --> 00:12:11,950
After the disaster, an official fire investigation was conducted and there it was concluded that the most likely perpetrator was a passenger on board

39
00:12:11,950 --> 00:12:16,216
named Erik Mørk Andersen, 37 years.

40
00:12:16,216 --> 00:12:27,150
He was previously convicted of murder.
However, he himself died in the flames after the second fire so you couldn't be sure it was he.

41
00:12:27,150 --> 00:12:39,466
An interesting investigation from 2006 by two fire engineers at Lund University of Technology concluded that there were not only two fires on board ..

42
00:13:22,716 --> 00:13:29,766
And the same day as the purchase, they assured the ship for $ 24 million.

43
00:13:29,766 --> 00:13:43,100
According to this theory, the company Sea Escape can thus be the cause of the fire and got some of the crew to set fire to the ship and later get the insurance money.

44
00:13:44,216 --> 00:13:52,133
Why did everything go so wrong then?
How could the fire on board get such a disastrous outcome?

45
00:13:52,133 --> 00:13:57,250
According to the Accident Investigation Board's report, this was due to several things.

46
00:13:57,250 --> 00:14:06,016
Partly that when the captain of the command bridge is notified of the fire, the alarm within the ship is incomplete.

47
00:14:06,016 --> 00:14:10,400
No proper attempt at all extinguish the fires was carried out…

48
00:14:10,400 --> 00:14:17,466
It was even so that the fire manager on board did not know that it was his task.

49
00:14:17,466 --> 00:14:27,716
There were seven smoke diver equipment on board, but no one was used to extinguish the fire or to save any passengers.

50
00:14:27,716 --> 00:14:32,200
3 of them were used in the evacuation of the ship.

1
00:01:41,716 --> 00:01:50,550
Fartyget lämnade hamnen i Oslo kl 21:45 lokal tid - 2 timmar och en kvart försenad.

2
00:01:50,550 --> 00:02:01,666
Resan skulle ha påbörjats redan 19:30 men arbetet med att få ombord personbilar och lastbilar tog längre tid än förväntat.

3
00:02:01,666 --> 00:02:14,683
Resan mot Fredrikshamn går smärtfritt till en början ända fram tills att klockan var mellan 01:45-02:00 på natten den 7 april.

4
00:02:14,683 --> 00:02:27,100
Fartyget var nu ute på öppet vatten i en del av Nordsjön som kallas för Skagerack och de flesta av passagerarna låg och sov.

5
00:02:28,583 --> 00:02:37,616
På däck 4 väcks plötsligt några passagerare ur sin sömn när de hör ett knastrande ljud ute i korridoren.

6
00:02:37,616 --> 00:02:49,216
Några dörrar bort ligger det en hög med sängkläder på golvet som brinner. Som tur är så lyckas de att släcka branden tillsammans med besättningen.

7
00:02:49,216 --> 00:02:57,066
En av besättningsmedlemmarna gick upp till kommandobryggan och meddelade förste styrman som just då hade vakten.

8
00:02:57,066 --> 00:03:07,766
Han gick i sin tur och meddelade till kaptenen om vad som hade hänt och sa till kaptenen att “Det är någon som leker pyroman”.

9
00:03:07,766 --> 00:03:17,100
Efter det att kaptenen Hugo Larsen blev meddelad så sändes förste styrman ned till brandplatsen för att kontrollera.

10
00:03:17,100 --> 00:03:28,783
Man såg till att att var ordentligt släckt och städade upp.
Efter det ringde förste styrmannen upp till kaptenen på bryggan igen och meddelade att allt var under kontroll.

11
00:03:29,700 --> 00:03:44,100
Men det hela slutade inte där. Någon gång strax efter kl 02:00 uppstod en till brand på däck 3 utanför en hytt i en korridor på styrbords sida.

12
00:03:44,100 --> 00:03:57,316
Detta var i närheten till trappan som leder upp till däck 4 och 5. Inom några få minuter hade branden spridit sig så pass mycket att hela korridoren stod i lågor

13
00:03:57,316 --> 00:04:05,066
och tjock rök letade sig upp i trapphuset och började att fylla korridorerna på däck 4 och 5.

14
00:04:05,066 --> 00:04:15,350
Det uppstod larm från ett flertal olika brandlarmsknappar i korridorerna på däck 4 och 5 när passagerarna där hade upptäckt branden.

15
00:04:15,350 --> 00:04:31,200
När kaptenen fick vetskapen om detta var klockan ca 02:15 och när förste styrman kom in på bryggan så fick han order från kapten att sända ut signalen “BRANDLARM” över hela fartyget.

16
00:04:31,200 --> 00:04:41,116
Kaptenen utlöste självstängningen av branddörrarna inom de områden där brandlarmsknapparna hade tryckts in av passagerarna.

17
00:04:41,116 --> 00:04:51,883
Men eftersom ingen knapp hade tryckts in där branden startade på styrbordssidan av däck 3 så lämnades branddörrarna där öppna.

18
00:04:51,883 --> 00:05:05,033
Väggarna och taket på däck 3 var täckta med plastlaminat och när det brann där skapade det en rök som innehöll höga halter av vätecyanid och kolmonoxid

19
00:05:05,033 --> 00:05:14,033
och efter bara 10 minuter så hade korridorerna uppnått en dödlig koncentration av de båda gaserna.

20
00:05:16,983 --> 00:05:28,366
02:24 Man stängde nu av fartygets framdrivning och startade sen igång brandpumparna men branden var redan utom kontroll.

21
00:05:28,366 --> 00:05:42,583
Kaptenen Hugo Larsen skickade ut en nödsignal till Tjøme radio i Norge där man meddelade om branden ombord och att passagerarna och besättningen skulle nu börja röra sig mot livbåtarna.

22
00:05:43,183 --> 00:05:51,533
Ombord är det just nu total panik bland passagerarna. Många kämpar sig igenom de rökfyllda korridorerna.

23
00:05:51,533 --> 00:05:59,883
Vissa personer har redan dött av den giftiga röken och passagerarna får kliva över dem för att kunna ta sig fram.

24
00:09:37,700 --> 00:09:44,533
159 människor miste sitt liv den natten.

25
00:09:51,833 --> 00:09:59,833
De undersökningar som gjorts i efterhand av rättsmedicinska myndigheter visar de troligen dog snabbt.

26
00:09:59,833 --> 00:10:13,766
Det var en kombination av ett flertal orsaker, dels själva branden men också av hög koldioxidhalt samt den giftiga röken innehållandes kolmonoxid och vätecyanid.

27
00:10:13,766 --> 00:10:24,750
Man uppskattar att de passagerare som tog sig ut i korridorerna hade inte orkat eller kunnat ta sig fram till någon utgång innan de föll ihop på golvet.

28
00:10:24,750 --> 00:10:31,166
De flesta av de omkomna, vilket var 99 personer, var kvar i sina hytter.

29
00:10:31,166 --> 00:10:38,683
Ca 50 personer hittades i korridorerna och de flesta befann sig i akterut på Däck 5.

30
00:10:38,683 --> 00:10:48,233
323 personer räddades från Scandinavian Star den natten och av dem var bara ett 30-tal skadade.

31
00:10:48,233 --> 00:10:55,666
De flesta hade lindrig rökförgiftning eller andra lättare skador som stukningar och blåmärken.

32
00:10:55,666 --> 00:11:05,683
Några togs i land via helikopter och andra fördes med fartygen till Lysekil, Sandefjord, Fredriksstad och Fredrikshamn.

33
00:11:07,133 --> 00:11:18,083
11.55 på dagen bogserades Scandinavian Star till Lysekil och är framme 21:17 på kvällen.

34
00:11:18,083 --> 00:11:29,516
Dagen efter den 8 april kl 16:30 är branden äntligen släckt och de döda kan börjas att lyftas i land.

35
00:11:29,516 --> 00:11:42,816
Eftersom majoriteten av passagerarna var från Norge så transporterades de döda kropparna i stora vita kylbilar med poliseskort till rättsmedicinska institutet i Oslo.

36
00:11:43,750 --> 00:11:54,233
Två frågor dyker snabbt upp i huvudet.
Vem anlade bränderna och varför gick allt…så fel?

37
00:11:54,233 --> 00:12:00,733
Tråkigt nog så har man inte kunnat att fastslå vem eller vilka som anlade bränderna på fartyget.

38
00:12:00,733 --> 00:12:11,950
Efter katastrofen så genomfördes en officiell brandutredning och där kom man fram till att den mest sannolika gärningsmannen var en passagerare ombord

39
00:12:11,950 --> 00:12:16,216
vid namn Erik Mørk Andersen, 37 år.

40
00:12:16,216 --> 00:12:27,150
Han var nämligen tidigare dömd för mordbrand. Han dog dock själv i lågorna efter den andra branden så man kunde inte vara säker på att det var han.

41
00:12:27,150 --> 00:12:39,466
En intressant utredning från 2006 av två brandingenjörer vid Lunds Tekniska Högskola kom fram till att det inte bara var två bränder ombord..

42
00:13:22,716 --> 00:13:29,766
och samma dag som köpet så försäkrade dem fartyget för 24 miljoner dollar.

43
00:13:29,766 --> 00:13:43,100
Enligt den här teorin så kan alltså företaget Sea Escape vara orsaken till branden och fått en del av besättningen att sätta eld på fartyget för att senare få ut försäkringspengarna.

44
00:13:44,216 --> 00:13:52,133
Varför gick allt så fel då? Hur kunde branden ombord få ett sånt katastrofalt utfall?

45
00:13:52,133 --> 00:13:57,250
Enligt haverikommisionens rapport så berodde detta på flera saker.

46
00:13:57,250 --> 00:14:06,016
Dels att när kaptenen på kommandobryggan får besked om branden så är alarmeringen inom fartyget ofullständig.

47
00:14:06,016 --> 00:14:10,400
Inget ordentligt försök till alla släcka bränderna genomfördes…

48
00:14:10,400 --> 00:14:17,466
Det var till och med så att brandchefen ombord visste inte att det var hans uppgift.

49
00:14:17,466 --> 00:14:27,716
Det fanns sju stycken rökdykarutrustningar ombord, men ingen användes för att släcka elden eller att rädda några passagerare.

50
00:14:27,716 --> 00:14:32,200
Man använde 3 av dem vid utrymningen av skeppet.

9

10
00:01:34,680 --> 00:01:41,460
Bigfoot is a large alar -like creature that is said to be in the forests in North America.

11
00:01:41,460 --> 00:01:46,880
It goes on two legs, which we humans do and have a dark coat.

12
00:01:46,880 --> 00:01:50,840
The body should be very muscular and broad -axled.

13
00:01:50,840 --> 00:01:55,820
The length of Bigfoot is somewhere between 2-3 meters.

14
00:01:55,820 --> 00:02:04,480
Bigfoot leaves large human -like footprints behind.
Hence the name..bigfoot

15
00:02:04,480 --> 00:02:16,220
Those who are said to have seen Bigfoot say that the face has character traits similar to a person's but that it also resembles a gorillas.

16
00:02:16,220 --> 00:02:25,040
Bigfoot should also have a very unpleasant and peculiar smell.
A stench that feels at a very long distance.

17
00:02:25,040 --> 00:02:29,000
Bigfoot is what is called a cryptozoolological creature.

18
00:02:29,000 --> 00:02:36,540
It is a collective name for a number of different animal species that have not been proven by science.

19
00:02:36,540 --> 00:02:49,800
Examples of these are Storsjöodjuret, Loch Ness beast, Chupacabra, Yeti [Snowman] and others.

00:02:49,800 --> 00:02:58,460
The most common theory that flourishes about bigfoot is that it is a kind of undetected species of a primate.

21
00:06:27,580 --> 00:06:36,400

We go through it in a little while.
